# dsh-tool-tsfork — Go-native TypeScript compiler devices for DeepSeek Harness

A standalone package, installable as **one plugin** (two device tools) for the
DeepSeek Harness: mod

el-facing devices over a **parked Go-native TypeScript
compiler** — the can1357/TypeScript
perf fork

(`perf/checker-speedups-v3`, TS `7.1.0-dev`). `tsfork_status`
reports the binary, version banner an

d build stamp; `tsfork_check` runs
one-shot `-b` project-graph checks with parsed diagnostics, wall

time, and a
GOMAXPROCS cap. The compiler binary is built once and parked on the host; the
plugin onl
y speaks the harness device seam — zero upstream harness changes.
| Identity | Value |

| Package | `@hy-sde-org/dsh-tool-tsfork` |
| Plugin id | `hy-sde-tsfork` |
| Devices | `tsfork_stat
us` · `tsfork_check` (device-catalog tools via `dyn`) |

> **Based on can1357/TypeScript**
> (`perf/checker-speedups-v3`, a Go rewrite of
> microsoft/TypeScr

ipt, Apache-2.0
> lineage): no compiler code is ported or modified — this package is original
> plug

in code that spawns the binary once per call over a stable CLI contract
> (`tsc -b`, JSON-free defau

lt output). Adapted, not ported: the harness
> device seam (`device: true` tools via `ctx.tools` + `

ctx.systemPrompt`)
> exists so a deployment can expose a fast compiler without touching the
> repo's

pinned toolchain. See
> THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md.
## Why

The type gate on a large workspace is the stock `tsc -b` over the whole
solution graph — on the fork

harness's 337-project host graph that was
**54.25s cold** (91.6s CPU, 4.6GB peak), and every agent

that wants a
typecheck pays it serially. The Go compiler checks the same graph
byte-identically (pro

ject listings, 14/14 planted errors, deterministic
output) in **7.05s cold / ~0.6s warm** — 7.7× les

s wall time, 3.4× less CPU.
But nothing in a harness exposes it: gates run through `pnpm` scripts pi

nned
to `typescript@6.0.3`, and a plugin cannot replace a repo's own toolchain —
nor should it, beca

use oxlint `typeAware` and the typert generator need the
JS API that TS 7 (a Go binary) does not shi

p. What agents need is a *device*
pointing at a parked binary: loadable per deployment, unloadable b

y toggling
one row, structured output, no PATH tricks, no upstream changes — while the
pinned toolch
ain stays exactly as pinned.

ss installation with the device catalog (the package's peer
baseline is `@deepseek-ai/cordis ~4.0.5-

alpha.1`,
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` / `@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt`
`^0.2.1-alpha.2`; registries w

e host (default `~/.dsh/tsfork/tsc`)
with a `VERSION` stamp beside it — build it once from a checkou

ackage into the profile with an absolute `file:`
path — `pnpm add file:<abs-path-to-package>` in the

profile dir, then add
`@hy-sde-org/dsh-tool-tsfork` to `dsh.profile.bundles`. The package's own
`ds
h.bundle.patch` mounts the `hy-sde-tsfork` row.

### Run

Start the harness (`dsh web`) and ask the agent to check or probe a graph.
The model-facing calls (d
evice catalog — `dyn search tsfork`):

- `tsfork_status` (no arguments) — resolved binary, `Version 7.1.0-dev`
banner, build stamp from `<b

inaryDir>/VERSION`, 20s health probe.
- `tsfork_check` — `tsc -b <project>`; returns `exitCode`, `wa

llMs`,
`errorCount`/`warningCount`, parsed `diagnostics` (`file:line:col TSxxxx`),
an `outputTail`,

and a reproducible `command`. `dry: true` prepends
`--dry` (list the projects a build would run, wit

hout building). Pass
`cwd` (and `project`) explicitly outside the deployment's default checkout.

## What the bundle does

The plugin's `cordis.patch.yml` mounts **one plain agent-plane row**
(`hy-sde-tsfork`) that consumes

the deployment's host services — `tools` and
`systemPrompt` (the stock agent bundle provides both).

No service, realm, or
filesystem seam of its own: each call spawns the parked compiler once, so
con

current agent lanes are isolated by construction and the only shared-box
knob is GOMAXPROCS. It also

registers the `tsfork:tools` prompt section,
which documents the buildinfo gotcha and the adoption

boundary to every
session that mounts the device.
## Engine behavior

- **One-shot spawn, stdin closed.** Every call is `spawn(binary, argv)` with
`stdio: ['ignore', 'pip

e', 'pipe']` — the compiler never reads stdin, and
a held-open pipe is the classic CLI-wrapper hang.

- **Flag order.** The Go parser requires `-b`/`--build` to precede the
project path; post-project f

lags (`--dry`, …) are accepted after it. A
[该节后续省略]
## Privacy and security notes

- **No network.** The plugin spawns a local binary; it sends nothing
off-host and holds no credentia

ls.
- **No shell layer.** Every input (project, extra args) is its own argv
element — a hostile stri

ng stays inert. `project` must resolve to an
existing tsconfig (or directory containing one) or the

call is rejected.
- **Environment.** The child inherits the host env with at most one
override (`GOM
AXPROCS`); no secrets are added or redacted by the plugin.
## Compatibility

- Node.js ≥ 22.19.0.
- DeepSeek Harness peer range: `@deepseek-ai/cordis ~4.0.5-alpha.1`,
`@deepseek

-ai/dsh-tools ^0.2.1-alpha.2`,
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt ^0.2.1-alpha.2`.
- Seam contract: `de

vice: true` tool registration (`tsfork_status`,
`tsfork_check`) + a `systemPrompt` section; registri

es without the device
concept present the same tools eagerly.
